notes: kb/Work PB5160 landed. §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1: a nonnumeric literal is 'delimited at the beginning and at the end by the separator quotation mark'; the apostrophe became a quotation symbol in 2002 (§2002:F.2 item 3, 'Apostrophe as quotation symbol'). LiteralScreen.GateFormat now asks CobolLiteral.IsApostropheDelimited of every literal token (the opening delimiter after any prefix) and refuses one below 2002 through the construct apostrophe-quotation-symbol-2002 (COBOL0900, VCR row 7.72). Probed at --std 85: DISPLAY 'HI', MOVE 'DE', VALUE 'ABC', a level-88 VALUE 'XYZ', VALUE ALL 'Q', 'ABC''D' and X'4142' are each COBOL0900 'the apostrophe-delimited literal'; "IT'S" (an apostrophe as content) runs; at 2002 every one runs. The rest of the format held as the read recorded (one character, 160 characters over three continued lines, doubled quotation marks; the empty literal refused). Residual outside the literal rule: a token gate sees the literals of the replaced text, so an apostrophe-delimited text-word that a REPLACE operand matches and replaces before lexing is not seen (the X"..." and zero-length gates share it); reported as a lead of wave 20262029 group G.

next.reason: 1985 writes a nonnumeric literal "{character-1} ...": braces, so at least one character, and only the quotation mark delimits it (SR2 and GR2 name only the quotation mark). §2023:8.3.3.2.2 brackets it, " [character-1] … ", adds the apostrophe-delimited form ' [character-1] … ' and the X"…" hexadecimal form, and §2023:8.3.3.2.4 GR3 gives the empty case its meaning: "If character-1 is not specified, the literal is a zero-length literal." Every 1985 literal keeps its meaning; "" and apostrophe literals that 1985 refuses are accepted at compile time, with no exception condition.
